review_notes: Read the whole target file, plus the uses of f4OppositeRootIndex, f4Length_opposite and f4OppositeRootIndex_eq_reflectionPerm in the Algebra/Lie/F4 files, and the Length.lean lemmas. I did not run Lean. The existing simp lemmas f4OppositeRootIndex_f4OppositeRootIndex and f4OppositeRootIndex_castAdd look fine: both orient toward simpler forms and neither creates a cycle. I did not check whether Mathlib already has a general simp lemma for the root at a reflectionPerm-self index, and my grep for one was inconclusive. The findings concern missing simp coverage, so how much downstream simp behaviour changes is uncertain.

findings.excerpt:
theorem f4Length_opposite (α : Fin 48) :
    f4Length (f4OppositeRootIndex α) = f4Length α := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical normal-form lemma for `f4Length ∘ f4OppositeRootIndex`. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, although the other lemmas about the same operation are: `f4OppositeRootIndex_f4OppositeRootIndex`, `f4KillingRoot_f4OppositeRootIndex` and `f4ModularCoroot_f4OppositeRootIndex`. Callers therefore name it by hand, either in `rw [..., f4Length_opposite, ...]` or in `simp only [..., f4Length_opposite]`. The `simp only` call in Exponential.lean already treats it as a simp rewrite. Plain `simp` cannot eliminate `f4Length (f4OppositeRootIndex _)` anywhere else.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp] theorem f4Length_opposite`. The LHS is strictly larger than the RHS, so the rewrite terminates. It does not overlap with `f4OppositeRootIndex_castAdd`, which rewrites the inner argument to a `Fin.addNat` term; simp rewrites inside-out, so `f4Length_opposite` cannot match after that step.
findings.benefit: Calls like `rw [hβ, f4Length_opposite, hα] at hlen` and the `simp only [..., f4Length_opposite]` pre-processing in Exponential.lean can use the default simp set. A user then no longer has to remember which length lemma to cite. The `@[simp]` set for `f4OppositeRootIndex` also becomes consistent across the F4 development.

evidence.excerpt: f4Length_opposite] at hk <;> rw [f4Length_def] at hk <;> decide +revert

findings.excerpt:
theorem f4OppositeRootIndex_eq_reflectionPerm (α : Fin 48) :
    f4OppositeRootIndex α = f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.reflectionPerm α α := (rfl)
findings.problem: The file never states the fact that makes `f4OppositeRootIndex` useful in simp normal form: the pinned root at the opposite index is the negative, `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root (f4OppositeRootIndex α) = -f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root α`. `f4Length_opposite` re-derives it as a local `hroot`, written as `root α + (-2) • root α`. Downstream code reaches the negation fact by unfolding to `reflectionPerm` with `simpa only [f4OppositeRootIndex_eq_reflectionPerm]` and `root_eq_neg_iff`. That unfolding is repeated at two sites in ChevalleyAction.lean. The definition is not reducible, so `simp` cannot see through it, and the only bridge lemma, `f4OppositeRootIndex_eq_reflectionPerm`, is an unfolding lemma that is not intended as simp.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum_root_f4OppositeRootIndex (α : Fin 48) : f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root (f4OppositeRootIndex α) = -f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root α`. Prove it from `f4OppositeRootIndex_eq_reflectionPerm`, `root_reflectionPerm` and `reflection_apply_self`, the same simp-only set already used in `f4Length_opposite`. Then derive the `root β ≠ -root α ↔ β ≠ f4OppositeRootIndex α` form once, so that `hneg` is `by simpa using hopp` or an `injective`/`iff` lemma. Also use it in `f4Length_opposite` in place of the `hroot` block. The RHS is a smaller term, so the rewrite is cycle-free.
findings.benefit: The repeated `simpa only [f4OppositeRootIndex_eq_reflectionPerm] using ...root_eq_neg_iff.mp h` blocks collapse to a single lemma. Goals with `root (f4OppositeRootIndex α)` normalise to `-root α` by default, matching how `f4KillingRoot_f4OppositeRootIndex` already behaves for the Killing roots.
